A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRCORL despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward and cost measurements, inference timings, hyperparameter ablations and training curves in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, inference timings, additional ablations and training curves with stated multi-seed aggregation in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core diffusion regularization, Gaussian policy and gradient manipulation remain. Algorithm 1 removes continued diffusion updates and the explicit actor-pretraining step; Appendix B.1 explicitly freezes diffusion after pretraining. v2 removes the separate CRPO procedure and optional PID objective, and corrects cost equations, including r(s,a) to c(s,a) in the cost-critic target. The cost-only objective already appeared in v1's practical algorithm.

E1.justification: Reported evaluation expands from four velocity-control tasks to thirteen tasks. Table 1 and Appendix C add CarGoal1/2, PointGoal1/2, PointButton1, PointCircle1, CarRun, BallCircle and CarCircle, substantially broadening coverage to navigation and additional Bullet-Gym control tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CAPS and CCAC and changes the BC comparison to explicitly safe-trajectory BC-Safe. The inference comparison adds FISOR. BEARL matches the earlier BEAR-Lag, and TREBI matches the previously labelled Diffuser from Lin et al. (2023); these are renamings rather than additional comparators.

E3.justification: v1 Section 5.3 specifies cost limit l=10 for Table 1, whereas v2's table averages over three cost-limit scales, substantially changing the main comparison protocol. New CarRun experiments introduce slack-initialization and cost-limit sweeps. These are reported evaluation-design changes; the PDFs do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds CarRun sensitivity tests for initial slack values 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, plus training curves under cost limits 10, 20 and 30. These extend hyperparameter robustness analysis. The earlier HalfCheetah cost-limit and temperature-schedule analyses remain as Figures 2(b) and 3.

E5.justification: v1 contains shaded training traces without specifying seed counts or defining their statistical meaning. v2 Table 1 specifies five random seeds, and Appendix C.3 explicitly describes means and standard deviations across five independent seeds. This adds statistical reporting without establishing an increase from a previously stated run count.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include DRCORL return/cost pairs of 0.91/0.00 on CarGoal1 and 0.79/0.60 on CarGoal2. The four original DRCORL table entries remain unchanged, while other entries change: CDT HalfCheetah becomes 0.96/0.61 from 0.48/3.65. The revised cost-limit aggregation prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Appendix training traces are also replaced and expanded.

T1.justification: The principal propositions, theorem, assumptions and derivations are retained. However, v1 Appendix A.2 explicitly assigns weight 1/2 to aligned-gradient iterations; v2 omits this case from the weight definition following Equation 41, leaving that definition incomplete. The added discussion of omitting KL regularization supplies interpretation rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diffusion regularization enables efficient policy inference, and gradient manipulation balances reward with soft safety constraints. The new title and expanded experimental support do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: New discussion explains asymmetric reward/cost critic conservatism, gradient-conflict handling, the relevance of the idealized KL-free analysis and failure modes of overly fast or slow temperature growth. Pretraining overhead is elaborated, while dataset-quality and safety limitations were already acknowledged. v2 also newly describes temperature schedules as similarly effective despite retaining a caption favoring square-root growth.

D1.justification: v2 adds details about separate critics and obtaining gradients through saved policy parameters and independent critic-driven updates. It specifies linear slack decay, describes temperature growth from 0.04 to 1.0, supplies CAPS/CCAC hyperparameters and discloses 20 evaluation episodes. Most existing architecture and training-budget information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and related-work discussion substantially broaden coverage of recent safe RL methods, adding works on CAPS, CCAC, VOCE, FAWAC, SafeDiffuser, OASIS, Saformer and additional trust-region/gradient approaches. These expand positioning around safe diffusion, conditional modeling and constraint adaptation. The Tessler et al. (2018) reference is removed.

P1.justification: The practical-method explanation, experimental discussion, related work and conclusion are substantially rewritten or condensed. Computational efficiency becomes part of Section 5.1; the former Appendix C is incorporated into Appendix B, and experimental Appendix D is reorganized as Appendix C. A clarification subsection is added and the paper is retitled.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned with separate reward/cost columns and best-safe-policy highlighting, and both tables expand. Earlier Figures 2 and 3 become a combined figure; the temperature plot moves to the appendix. New ablation plots and numerous redrawn or added training curves substantially change the visual presentation. Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 also adopt compact text-wrapped layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis for the claimed reward-safety balance beyond v1's four locomotion tasks, adding navigation tasks and stronger safe baselines. Explicit multi-seed variability and implementation details improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized regressions, particularly the omitted aligned-gradient weight in Appendix A.2 and the inconsistent temperature discussion. Changed aggregation means revised scores should not be read as same-setting performance improvements.
